doc.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Will he keep the big band going? Staying in shape
summary: A trombonist fears it may be over; Rendón, who has led the band since 2012, is determined to keep it, practicing daily at home.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I wonder, if this goes on for longer than we hope, are there things you’re doing, I guess I’m referring to the big band, and the energy and time you put — I mean I’ll set this up. I remember you talking about one of your chores as a band leader and that is putting the music back in the folders in the right order, and what a job that is.
So I’m wondering if you might get to the point where because you can’t possibly do this now, you might consider do I want to do it again?

I’ve thought about that. I’ve thought about whether as a matter of fact — I had a conversation with one of my trombone players, he called me out of the blue, and he was saying, “This might be it for us. Is it over? Am I done?” You know, “Am I going to play again?” But I don’t want to give up. I’ve had the band now since 2012, that’s going on 13 years in September. I would like to have the band into my later age for at least, give it another ten, fifteen years, if I can hold on to it. It’s not easy, but as soon as I get the opportunity I’m just going to jump right back in. I’m keeping myself in shape by walking

every day and doing a little bit of exercise, I’ve been practicing. For two months I couldn’t go to my practice studio to practice, you know, play the drums. But I stayed home and I practiced two, three hours, you know just doing rudiments and hand exercises and my chops are actually feeling good. So no, I’m going to hang in there. It’s a baby that I gave birth to and I’m not going to let it go that easy you know. I’m determined.
